page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. The underlying hardware features an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. This configuration allocates 2 threads per core across 1 physical core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and AES instructions. Local storage is provided via a bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier, whereas multi-core performance falls into the average category. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show strong results, with gzip compression reaching 32.12 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 14.64 GB/sec. However, overall PassMark CPU metrics, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests, are positioned in the weak tier. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block read and write bandwidths are average, small-block cached read bandwidth is weak.

The instance exhibits performance limitations in high-throughput scenarios. Static web serving throughput is poor, registering at 2.3 GB/sec, and database operations under PassMark and Redis SET benchmarks are weak. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference text generation with a small 135M model achieves an average speed of 121.47 tokens/sec, but drops to a poor 5.0 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. Given the shared CPU allocation and high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core CPU performance. It is suitable for caching layers, lightweight memory-bound applications, and basic development environments.
description: The Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is an x86_64 server in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 2 shared vCPUs on 1 physical AMD EPYC core, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a 100 GB NVMe SSD. Operating at 2.0 GHz, the processor supports AVX-512 and cryptographic instructions. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and strong single-threaded compression speeds. However, multi-core performance, PassMark CPU scores, and database operations are weak, and static web serving throughput is poor. The high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core makes this instance qualitatively cost-effective for memory-intensive, non-compute-heavy workloads. It is best suited for caching, lightweight memory-bound applications, and development environments.
